plain: Historical prices rescaled for share splits and dividends, so a chart shows what an investor really experienced rather than fake jumps.
desk: Always backtest on adjusted closes.

plain: Being traded against by someone who knows more than you. The trades you get are the ones you'd rather not have.
desk: Everything we bought this morning went down: classic adverse selection.

plain: Unusual data, like satellite images, card spending or web traffic, used to spot trends before official figures come out.
desk: The alt data's pointing to a weak quarter.

plain: A group of things you can buy that behave in a similar way and make money in a similar way: equities, bonds, FX, commodities, derivatives.
desk: Gold's had a better year than any other asset class.

plain: A firm hired to invest someone else's money for a fee: hedge funds, long-only funds, private equity.
desk: We're one of their three external managers.

plain: Whoever actually owns the money: pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, family offices. They often hire asset managers to invest it.
desk: The big asset owners are cutting hedge fund allocations.

plain: How much money a fund manager looks after for its clients.
desk: They're running about 20 billion of AUM.

plain: A line a curve gets closer and closer to but never touches.
How governments usually sell new bonds: they say how much they want to borrow, investors put in bids, and the best bids win.
desk: The 10-year auction tailed, so yields jumped.

plain: The number being multiplied over and over. In 2 to the power x, the base is 2.
One hundredth of 1%. So 25 basis points is 0.25%.
desk: The Bank hiked 25 bps.

plain: The index a fund is measured against, like the FTSE 100 or S&P 500.
desk: We beat the benchmark by 2% this year.

plain: A broker's duty to get its client the best overall result: price, cost, speed and the chance of the trade actually happening.
desk: Compliance wants to see the best-ex report.

plain: The gap between the price a market maker will buy at (the bid) and sell at (the ask). It's how market makers earn their money.
desk: The spread's blown out to 3 pips.

plain: Collecting orders from big investors (how many shares or bonds, at what price) to decide the price of a new issue.
desk: The book's covered three times over.

plain: The biggest global investment banks that do everything: advice, new issues, trading, research and prime brokerage.
desk: She's at a bulge bracket on the FX desk.

plain: Firms that invest money and are paid according to how their investments do: hedge funds, pension funds, fund managers.
desk: He moved from the sell side to the buy side.

plain: Lots of people trying to buy at once, pushing the price up. The opposite is selling pressure.
desk: Real buying pressure in gold today.

plain: Compound annual growth rate: the steady yearly rate that takes you from a start value to an end value.
desk: The fund's done 11% CAGR over five years.

plain: The event that will make the market see what you see and move the price, like results day or a central bank meeting.
desk: What's the catalyst, and when?

plain: A firm that steps in between buyer and seller and guarantees both sides, so neither loses out if the other goes bust.
desk: It's cleared, so we're not worried about the other side.

plain: Earning returns on your returns, so each period's gain becomes part of what grows next.
desk: Over 30 years, compounding does most of the work.

plain: The average forecast from analysts: what the market expects. Results are judged against it.
desk: Profits came in 5% above consensus.

plain: One feed that combines the quotes and trades from every venue into a single official record.
desk: The print showed up on the tape a moment later.

plain: The interest a bond pays each year, usually as a percentage of what you lent. A 5% coupon on 100 pounds pays 5 pounds a year.
desk: It's a 10-year with a 4% coupon.

plain: A trading venue that hides orders until after they've traded, so big orders don't move the price.
desk: We got half the order done in the dark.

plain: A firm that quotes prices and trades with clients using its own money, taking the other side of the deal.
desk: Three dealers came back on the RFQ.

plain: A growth factor below 1, so each period keeps only part of what was there.
Part of a bonus paid over the next few years and lost if you leave early. Often called golden handcuffs.
desk: Half my bonus is deferred over three years.

plain: How much people want to buy at each price. Drawn as the buyers line, which slopes down.
desk: Demand for dollars is strong this morning.

plain: How much a matrix scales area. 2 means areas double; 0 means everything gets squashed flat onto a line.
Market data bought straight from one exchange, arriving faster than the consolidated tape.
desk: The HFTs are all on the direct feeds.

plain: The growth you give up by waiting. Used to shrink future money back to what it's worth today.
desk: We're discounting at 6%.

plain: Part of a company's profit paid out to the people who own its shares.
desk: They've raised the dividend again.

plain: How far a portfolio has fallen from its highest point.
desk: He's in a 6% drawdown, so risk is cutting his gross.

plain: A reason you'll be right when the market is wrong: better information, better interpretation, or more speed.
desk: What's your edge on this trade?

plain: The idea that prices already reflect available information, so beating the market consistently is hard. Comes in weak, semi-strong and strong versions.
desk: In a market this efficient, any edge has to come from somewhere others aren't looking.

plain: A central, regulated marketplace where standardised things trade under the same public rules for everyone.
desk: It's listed on the exchange, so the price is right there on the screen.

plain: Shrinking where each step multiplies by the same number below 1. It gets close to zero but never reaches it.
Growth where each step multiplies by the same number, so it grows faster the bigger it gets.
An average where older data gets exponentially smaller weights, so recent days count most.
desk: We use an EWMA vol with lambda 0.94.

plain: Each firm in the chain between a saver and the market taking its own fee, so the costs stack up.
desk: After fee layering, the pension kept barely half the gain.

plain: Fixed income, currencies and commodities: the part of a bank's trading floor that isn't equities.
desk: FICC revenues were up on the quarter.

plain: The same thing trading on many venues at once, so its buyers and sellers are spread across lots of order books.
desk: Liquidity's so fragmented you need a router just to find it.

plain: An independent firm that works out what a fund is worth and keeps its investor records, so investors don't rely on the manager's word.
desk: The administrator signs off the monthly NAV.

plain: A bond issued by the UK government, sold at auctions run by the Debt Management Office.
desk: Gilts sold off after the budget.

plain: Longs plus shorts as a percentage of the fund's own money. Above 100% means it's using borrowed money.
desk: We're running 180% gross.

plain: What you multiply by each period. 5% growth is a growth factor of 1.05.
A fund that tries to make money whichever way markets go. It can bet on falls, borrow to invest more, and charges a share of profits.
desk: The fund's net short going into earnings.

plain: The previous peak. After losses, a manager must get back above it before earning performance pay again.
desk: She's below her high-water mark, so no payout yet.

plain: The rate at which prices rise, so each pound (or naira) buys a bit less each year.
desk: UK inflation came in at 3%.

plain: A company's first sale of shares to the public, when it lists on a stock exchange and the company gets the money.
desk: The IPO popped 30% on day one.

plain: Whoever creates and first sells a share or bond: a company or a government. It gets the money from the first sale.
desk: The issuer's coming back for more next month.

plain: A formula for the bet size that grows money fastest, given your odds. Traders usually bet only a fraction of it.
desk: We size at quarter Kelly.

plain: The delay between something happening in the market and you seeing it, or reacting to it.
desk: We cut our latency to under ten microseconds.

plain: An investor who puts money into a fund but doesn't run it. The fund manager is the general partner (GP).
desk: The LPs want lower fees.

plain: How easily you can buy or sell without moving the price much. Lots of buyers and sellers means liquid; few means illiquid.
desk: Liquidity's thin going into the holidays.

plain: A trading venue that shows orders to everyone before they trade.
desk: Small orders go lit, the block goes dark.

plain: A fund that only buys (never bets on falls) and is judged against a benchmark like the S&P 500.
desk: Long-only money has been selling tech.

plain: A fee model that pays a small rebate to orders that wait in the book and charges a fee to orders that trade straight away.
desk: Post passively and collect the rebate.

plain: Anywhere buyers and sellers meet and agree a price. It can be a car boot sale, a website or a network of banks.
desk: FX is a 24-hour market with no building.

plain: What a whole company is worth at today's share price: the price times the number of shares.
desk: It's a 50 million market cap, so it's small.

plain: The stream of quotes and trades a market produces, plus its history.
desk: Our market data bill went up again.

plain: How much is waiting to be bought and sold at each price beyond the best ones. Shown by Level 2 data.
desk: There's no depth: one big order and it'll gap.

plain: A firm that always quotes a price to buy and a price to sell, earning the gap and trying not to hold a big position either way.
desk: The market makers pulled their quotes in the sell-off.

plain: The price where the amount people want to buy equals the amount people want to sell. Also called the equilibrium price.
desk: Where's the market in gold right now?

plain: Important facts that aren't public yet. Trading on them is insider dealing, a crime.
desk: You're wall-crossed, so you can't trade it.

plain: A grid of numbers that acts like a machine: feed it an arrow and it hands you back a new one.
desk: Multiply through by the sensitivity matrix.

plain: A firm that hands money to many independent PM teams (pods), each with its own strict risk limits.
desk: She left the single-manager for a pod shop.

plain: The best price to sell at and the best price to buy at across all US exchanges at that moment.
desk: We filled inside the NBBO.

plain: Longs minus shorts as a percentage of the fund's own money: how much of a market move the fund catches.
desk: We're 40% net long into the data.

plain: Open, high, low, close and volume for each period: the data behind a candlestick chart.
desk: Just pull daily OHLCV for the last ten years.

plain: Trading done directly between two parties, usually a client and a dealer, with no central order book.
desk: Most of the bond market is OTC.

plain: Buying a fund that simply copies an index, at very low cost, instead of trying to beat it.
desk: Passive flows are propping up the index.

plain: The person who decides what goes in a portfolio, how big each position is, and when to cut.
desk: Pitch it to the PM at the morning meeting.

plain: What money you'll get later is worth today.
desk: PV of that cash flow is about seven and a half k.

plain: The market finding the price by pulling buyers and sellers together, rather than anyone deciding it.
desk: The first hour after the news is all price discovery.

plain: News the market already expected, so it's already reflected in the price. Only surprises move it.
desk: The rate cut was fully priced in.

plain: Where brand-new shares or bonds are sold for the first time. The issuer gets the money.
desk: Primary's been busy with new bond deals this week.

plain: The part of a bank that serves hedge funds: lending them money and shares, holding their assets and settling their trades.
desk: Our prime broker raised the margin on that position.

plain: Firms that buy whole companies with investors' money and borrowed money, improve them, and sell them a few years later.
desk: It's PE-owned, so they'll look to sell in a few years.

plain: Buying and selling to get a portfolio back to its target mix after prices have moved.
desk: Month-end rebalancing flows hit the dollar.

plain: Asking a few dealers for their price, then dealing with whoever's best.
desk: Put it out to five dealers on RFQ.

plain: The most a buyer would pay, or the least a seller would accept, before walking away.
desk: He won't sell below 98: that's his reservation price.

plain: The extra return investors expect for putting up with more risk. It's why bumpier assets that pay income have usually paid more over time.
desk: The equity risk premium looks thin at these prices.

plain: Where investors trade existing shares and bonds with each other. The issuer gets nothing from these trades.
desk: The new bonds are trading well in the secondary.

plain: Firms that sell financial services (advice, new issues, trading, lending, research) and are paid fees and spreads.
desk: Sell-side research is all bullish on it.

plain: A hedge fund where one founder makes the final call on every position.
desk: It's a single-manager shop, so the CIO decides everything.

plain: Software that checks prices, fees and speed on every venue and splits an order across them for the best overall result.
desk: The SOR sprayed it across six venues in a millisecond.

plain: A country's investment fund, often built from oil money or trade surpluses, investing for future generations.
desk: A sovereign wealth fund took a big chunk of the deal.

plain: A crypto token designed to always be worth the same as a normal currency, usually one US dollar.
desk: Clients are settling in dollar stablecoins.

plain: How much people are willing to sell at each price. Drawn as the sellers line, which slopes up.
desk: Supply cuts are pushing oil higher.

plain: The value a trade creates: the gap between what the buyer would pay at most and what the seller would accept at least.
desk: Both sides walked away with some of the surplus.

plain: Every individual quote and trade, timestamped: the most detailed price history there is.
desk: You'll need tick data to test anything intraday.

plain: The thing a derivative's price comes from. For a gold future, the underlying is gold.
desk: Where's the underlying trading?

plain: An investment bank that runs a new issue of shares or bonds, finds the buyers and helps set the price.
desk: We're one of three underwriters on the deal.

plain: A specific, evidence-backed view that differs from the consensus, with a reason the market will come round to it.
desk: What's your variant perception here?

plain: An arrow, or just a list of numbers like [2, 1].
desk: Send me the positions vector.

plain: How much a price jumps around. Usually measured as the standard deviation of returns.
desk: Vol's picked up since the data.
